March 31, 2026
Due to continued volatility in the fuel market and to maintain pricing accuracy and transparency, DHL will implement weekly fuel surcharge updates starting April 13 and continuing until further notice.
This change affects only the update frequency. The fuel surcharge calculation method, including the fluctuating 20-day rolling US Gulf Coast (USGC) average and the published fuel surcharge table, remains unchanged.
We are taking every step to protect our customers from unnecessary cost fluctuations and to ensure fair and predictable pricing.

DHL Express Announces Annual Price Adjustments in the U.S.
Press Release: Plantation, Fla., September 25, 2026
Average rate increase of 5.9%, will be effective as of January 1, 2027
DHL Express, the world’s leading international express services provider, announced a 5.9% general average shipment price adjustment for U.S. account holders that will take effect on January 1, 2027. A limited number of services and surcharges will also be adjusted.
DHL Express adjusts its prices annually to account for inflationary pressures, currency fluctuations, and industry-specific cost developments. As an internationally integrated business operating in more than 220 countries and territories, DHL Express is influenced not only by local economic conditions but also by developments across global markets.

DHL Express continues to invest in its global network, fleet modernization, digital capabilities, security infrastructure and sustainable logistics solutions to strengthen operational resilience and deliver a reliable shipping experience for customers. These investments support the ongoing evolution of the international express network while helping DHL meet the changing needs of businesses and consumers.

Effective 1 November 2026, Product Identifiers (PIDs) become a mandatory customs data element for Business-to-Consumer (B2C) shipments with a value of up to EUR 150 imported into the European Union (EU27). Introduced under the EU Customs Reform, this requirement aims to enhance product traceability, strengthen consumer protection, and support customs authorities in identifying non-compliant products entering the EU.
A Product Identifier (PID) is a unique alphanumeric code used to identify a specific product and improve traceability throughout the supply chain. Product Identifiers enable customs authorities to identify products more accurately and link them to manufacturers and merchants responsible for placing them on the market.
To support customs clearance for B2C shipments entering the EU27, the following Product Identifiers are required at line-item level:
| Product Identifier Type | Requirement |

| Merchant PID | Mandatory Required at line-item level for all B2C shipments entering the EU27. |
| Non-Standardized Manufacturer PID | Mandatory Required at line-item level for all B2C shipments entering the EU27. |
| Standardized Manufacturer PID | Optional (if available) May include a GTIN, EAN, or UPC and should be provided where available. |
Merchant PID: A product identifier assigned by the seller or merchant to distinguish a product within their catalogue.
Non-Standardized Manufacturer PID: A product identifier assigned by the manufacturer where no standardized identifier (such as GTIN, EAN, or UPC) is available.
The PID requirement has been introduced as part of the EU Customs Reform programme to strengthen customs oversight, improve product traceability, and address compliance challenges associated with high-volume e-commerce imports. The additional data helps customs authorities identify products more efficiently and enhance supply chain transparency.

Shippers sending B2C goods to the European Union will be required to submit the mandatory Product Identifiers as part of the electronic shipment data. If the required mandatory Product Identifier information is not provided, customs clearance may be delayed, rejected by customs authorities, or result in the shipment being returned to origin (RTO).
No. The Product Identifier requirement is an EU regulatory requirement and is not specific to DHL Express. All express carriers will require the necessary data to complete customs clearance.
The requirement becomes mandatory on 1 November 2026 for all applicable B2C imports into the EU27.
Shipments may be delayed, held by customs authorities, or returned to origin if the required PID information is missing

Complying with the EU PID requirements is essential for smooth customs clearance of B2C shipments entering the EU27. DHL Group continues its growth trajectory in the third quarter and
significantly increases revenue and earnings
 Group revenue increased 12.6 percent to EUR 22.7 billion
(Q3 2025: EUR 20.1 billion)
 Operating profit (EBIT) rose 16.2 percent to EUR 1.7 billion
(Q3 2025: EUR 1.5 billion)
 Free cash flow (excluding M&A) reached EUR 2.7 billion after the first nine months

of the year (9M 2025: EUR 2.3 billion)
 Following the guidance increase in October, DHL Group expects operating profit of
more than EUR 7.0 billion and free cash flow (excluding M&A) of more than
EUR 3.2 billion for 2026
 CEO Tobias Meyer: “We successfully continued our growth trajectory in the third
quarter, delivering a significant increase in revenue and earnings. Our strong
operational performance enabled us to raise our full-year earnings guidance for the
second time this year.”
Bonn, November 5, 2026: DHL Group continued its strong business performance in the third quarter
of 2026. Group revenue increased 12.6 percent year-over-year to EUR 22.7 billion (Q3 2025: EUR 20.1
billion). Operating profit (EBIT) rose 16.2 percent to EUR 1.7 billion (Q3 2025: EUR 1.5 billion). The
EBIT margin improved to 7.6 percent (Q3 2025: 7.3 percent). Based on the continued positive earnings
momentum, the Group raised its full-year 2026 guidance to an operating profit of more than EUR 7.0
billion (previously: more than EUR 6.5 billion) on October 16 and announced its preliminary results.

The positive business performance was driven by growth across a wide range of regions and sectors,
particularly in DHL Express, DHL Global Forwarding, and DHL Supply Chain. DHL Express recorded
very strong earnings growth. With its targeted offering for time-critical heavy-weight shipments for
industrial customers, the division significantly increased transported weight, improving utilization of its
global network. Disciplined yield and capacity management, together with structural cost
improvements implemented over the past two years, further supported earnings performance.
Temporary capacity constraints in the international air freight market generated additional demand,
which DHL Express served through its own global network.
Press release
“We successfully continued our growth trajectory in the third quarter, delivering a significant increase in
revenue and earnings. Our strong operational performance enabled us to raise our full-year earnings
guidance for the second time this year. We remain focused on providing our customers with high service

quality and sufficient capacity. Even in challenging conditions, we help them access markets and unlock
new growth opportunities. That is why we are stepping up investments in our network and in new
logistics capabilities needed to tap into the markets of the future.”
Tobias Meyer, CEO DHL Group
Positive business performance supports cash flow
The strong operational performance is also reflected in cash flow. Free cash flow (excluding M&A)
reached EUR 901 million in the third quarter (Q3 2025: EUR 1.2 billion) – including net cash outflows
of EUR 256 million related to the U.S. tariffs (IEEPA). In the first nine months, DHL Group generated
free cash flow (excluding M&A) of EUR 2.7 billion (9M 2025: EUR 2.3 billion). Consolidated net profit
after non-controlling interests amounted to EUR 907 million in the third quarter (Q3 2025: EUR 840
million). Basic earnings per share reached EUR 0.82, up 9.6 percent from EUR 0.75 in the third quarter
of 2025.
Targeted investments address changing customer needs

Despite geopolitical uncertainty, global trade continues to grow, even as trade flows are shifting. In this
environment, customers benefit from DHL Group’s global presence and operational flexibility. In line
with Strategy 2030, the Group is further developing its service offering to address evolving customer
requirements and additional logistics needs. Through its strategic growth initiatives, DHL Group
focuses on regions and sectors where it expects particularly dynamic growth in customer demand.
These include Life Sciences & Healthcare, New Energy, E-commerce, and Data Center Logistics.
Capital expenditures on acquired assets (capex) amounted to EUR 897 million in the third quarter.
After the first nine months, capex totaled EUR 2.2 billion, up EUR 532 million compared with the prior-
year period. In Data Center Logistics, for example, DHL Supply Chain is investing in additional
warehouse locations in North America while also expanding its capacity in the Asia Pacific region. DHL
Group is combining expertise across multiple divisions to offer integrated end-to-end solutions for

data centers. In addition, the Group continues to invest in digitalization, automation, and the
capabilities of its existing network.
Press release
Guidance raised for the second time
Given the continued positive earnings momentum, particularly at DHL Express, DHL Global Forwarding,
and DHL Supply Chain, as well as initial signs of robust seasonal developments in the fourth quarter, DHL
Group raised its guidance for fiscal year 2026 for the second time on October 16.
The Group now expects operating profit (EBIT) of more than EUR 7.0 billion (previously: more than EUR
6.5 billion). EBIT for the DHL divisions is forecast at more than EUR 6.4 billion (previously: more than
EUR 5.9 billion). Expectations for Post & Parcel Germany, with EBIT of more than EUR 900 million, and
for Group Functions, at around EUR -400 million, remain unchanged.
Guidance for free cash flow (excluding M&A) was raised to more than EUR 3.2 billion (previously: around
EUR 3.0 billion). To capture additional growth opportunities, the Group plans capital expenditures on

acquired assets (capex) of around EUR 3.6 billion in 2026 (previously: EUR 3.0 billion to EUR 3.3 billion).
In March 2027, DHL Group will review its existing medium-term guidance of operating profit of more
than EUR 7.0 billion in a normalized economic environment.
“Our continued strong earnings and cash flow generation enable us to invest selectively in further growth.
We maintain a disciplined approach to capital allocation, strengthening the capabilities and
efficiency of our network.”
Melanie Kreis, CFO DHL Group

EU Customs Changes 2026: New €2 Handling Fee & Product Identifier Requirements from 1 November
Shipping goods to the European Union (EU)? Two important customs changes taking effect on 1 November 2026 will impact businesses selling directly to EU consumers.
As part of the EU Customs Reform, exporters must prepare for a new €2 EU Handling Fee and mandatory Product Identifier (PID) requirements for Business-to-Consumer (B2C) shipments entering the EU's 27 member states.
These changes affect businesses in Thailand and other non-EU countries, regardless of shipment value. Understanding the requirements early can help businesses manage shipping costs, prepare accurate customs documentation and avoid unnecessary clearance delays.
Here's what exporters need to know and how to prepare.
What Are the New EU Customs Changes from 1 November 2026?
Two key regulatory changes will affect B2C shipments imported into the EU:
- €2 EU Handling Fee A mandatory €2 fee per import customs declaration line item, regardless of shipment value.

- Product Identifier (PID) Mandatory product identification data must be provided for each applicable line item to support EU customs clearance.
Both requirements apply to B2C goods shipped from outside the EU to consumers across the EU27.
These are EU regulatory requirements, not DHL Express-specific requirements, and apply across express carriers.
1. EU Handling Fee: What Exporters Need to Know
From 1 November 2026, a mandatory €2 EU Handling Fee will apply per import customs declaration line item for B2C shipments entering the EU, regardless of the goods' value.
The fee is intended to help cover the increasing costs of customs supervision and processing as international e-commerce shipments continue to grow.
How is the €2 EU Handling Fee calculated?
The fee is calculated based on import customs declaration line items, rather than simply the number of parcels or individual product units.

Important: The EU Handling Fee is a mandatory regulatory charge imposed under EU legislation. It is not a DHL Express service fee.

Is the €2 EU Handling Fee the same as the €3 customs duty?
No. These are two separate charges.
Since 1 July 2026, the EU has applied a €3 customs duty per applicable declaration line item on low-value B2C imports valued at €150 or less, replacing the previous customs duty exemption.
From 1 November 2026, the additional €2 EU Handling Fee will apply to B2C shipments regardless of shipment value.
Applicable customs duties, VAT and other charges may also apply depending on the shipment.
Who pays the EU Handling Fee?
For shipments handled by DHL Express, the party responsible for paying the fee depends on the selected DHL Duty Billing Service.
DTP – Duty Tax Paid
The shipper pays the applicable import duties, taxes and customs-related charges, including the EU Handling Fee.
DTU – Duty Tax Unpaid
The importer or receiver in the EU is responsible for paying the applicable import duties, taxes and customs-related charges, including the EU Handling Fee, before delivery.

Businesses should communicate these payment arrangements clearly to customers to help avoid unexpected charges or delivery delays.
2. Product Identifier (PID): Mandatory Information for EU Customs Clearance
The second important change concerns the information businesses must provide when shipping goods to EU consumers.
From 1 November 2026, Product Identifiers (PIDs) become mandatory at the line-item level for B2C imports into the EU27, regardless of shipment value.
What is a Product Identifier (PID)?
A Product Identifier is a unique alphanumeric code used to identify a specific product throughout the supply chain.
It enables EU Customs authorities to identify products more accurately, support product traceability and assess compliance with EU requirements.
The regulation is intended to strengthen consumer protection and help customs authorities identify potentially unsafe or non-compliant goods entering the EU.
Which Product Identifiers are required?
Businesses should prepare the following product information:

For example, an online seller exporting electronic accessories to Germany may need to provide the product's SKU, manufacturer model number and relevant barcode identifier, where available.
Businesses can usually find these codes in their product catalogues, supplier documentation, product packaging or e-commerce platform records.
What happens if a Product Identifier is missing?
Incomplete or incorrect PID information may prevent customs authorities from processing the import declaration.
This can result in:
- Customs clearance delays
- Shipment holds at the EU border
- Potential return to origin
Important: Product Identifiers are mandatory EU regulatory data requirements applicable to all express carriers, not requirements introduced by DHL Express.
How Can Thai Exporters Prepare for the New EU Customs Rules?
To help ensure smoother shipping and customs clearance, businesses should take the following steps before 1 November 2026.
1. Review your product information

Check that each product has the required Merchant PID and Manufacturer PID information. Request missing product identifiers from suppliers where necessary.
2. Submit Product Identifiers electronically
Provide complete and accurate PIDs at line-item level when creating shipments through DHL Express Electronic Shipping Solutions, such as MyDHL+.
3. Ensure accurate customs documentation
Provide complete product descriptions, accurate declared values, applicable HS codes and Commercial or Proforma Invoice information electronically.
4. Confirm the correct receiver details
Include the importer's or receiver's correct name, email address and mobile phone number to support efficient customs processing.
5. Review import charges and billing arrangements
Understand how the €2 EU Handling Fee affects your shipping costs and confirm whether duties and taxes will be paid by the shipper or receiver.
Taking these steps can help reduce the risk of customs clearance delays and unexpected costs.
